parties:
Nurul Hasan Mia and others ----- Petitioners.
Vs. 
Kherode Sarker & others  ----- Opposite-parties.
full_judgment:
On 11-12-72 the 1st party petitioners filed a petition under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the Court of the S.D.O. Bhola on which, being satisfied that there was apprehension of the Breach of peace over harvesting of the paddy in the lands described in the petition of the petitioners, the S.D.O. drew up proceedings under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, attached the land and appointed O.C. Daulatkhan P.S. as Receiver. The S.D.O. asked both the parties to file written statements in their Claims. Subsequently the receiver was changed, and Adjutant Ansar Bhola was appointed as receiver and then Mr. A Hassan the Assistant, Ansar, was appointed as Receiver. Parties took time on several occasions to file written statements. Ultimately the case came up for hearing on 9-7-74 on which date also the first party prayed for time. Their petition for time was rejected and the learned Magistrate passed an order abating the proceedings under the provisions of P.O. 135 of 1972. 

 In the application filed by the 1st party petitioners in the Court of the SDO Bhola which gave rise to the proceedings under section 145 Cr.P.C. it was stated by the petitioners that after the revisional survey operation the disputed lands were diluviated in the Meghna and reformed in situ within 15 years on which the petitioners constructed their house. thereon and they have been residing there doing cultivation for a period more of than 12 years, Then interest in the disputed land was established by the judgment passed on 30-11-68 in Title Suit No. 408 of 1968 in the Court of the Local Munsif. The petitioners grew paddy in the lands in 1379 B S. also but as the 2nd party men where threatening to take away the paddy forcibly, so the petitioners filed the application before the SDO praying for restraining the OPs. under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure from reaping the paddy grown by the petitioners in the disputed land. 

 5 Under P.O. 135 of 1972 old section 86 of the Stale Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was replaced by a new Section which runs thus :-- 

 (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the right, title and interest of the tenant or his successors-in-interest shall be extinguished in such land or port ion thereof, whether the loss of such lands or portion by diluvion took or fakes place before or after the commencement of the Stale Acquisition and Tenancy (Fourth Amendment) Order, 1972. 

 Explanation- For the purpose of this section the word "Family" shall have the same meaning as in clause (a) of section 151J, as amended by the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Fourth) Order, 1972". 

 6. If the disputed lands re-appeared in more than 12 years before filing of the application by the petitioners and they have been in possession of the same since such reappearance being recognized by the landlord, the provisions of sub-sec. (3) of P.O. 135 of 1972 will not be applicable in respect of the disputed lands. The petitioners did not make out any case of re-possession of the lands. On re-appearance, according to their case as already stated above, the lands reformed in situ more than 12 years before filing of the application by the petitioners and they have been in possession of the same since then. If the petitioners case as made out in their application be true then the sub-section (5) of P.O. 135 of 1972 will not also be attracted in the present case, Hence, without taking evidence on the point it cannot be said if the provisions of P.O. 135 of 1972 are applicable in the present case.
